correctness.summary: Equality in the BHM single-class comparison is characterized by an auxiliary tree with codegree one on every auxiliary edge. Equality in both bipartition classes then forces maximum degree at most two; even cycles are excluded by a cyclic auxiliary graph or, for C4, by codegree two. The lazy gap-transfer inequality follows from zero-edge contraction and the positive-probability no-zero event, and completes the unique-maximizer classification.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The direct 2026 source proves the non-strict BHM and LNR expectation inequalities and gives lazy strictness on cyclic graphs, but does not state the complete equality classifications or the standard-to-lazy gap transfer. Exact and synonymous searches found no coverage. The complete 2016 tree paper was not inspected in full, leaving a stated residual risk for a tree-only equality remark, and very recent parallel work remains possible.

value.summary: The result upgrades both newly completed path-extremality inequalities to uniqueness, isolates the exact auxiliary obstruction responsible for strictness, and supplies a quantitative gap-transfer inequality for every connected bipartite graph.

limitations: Originality is only to the best of our knowledge.
The complete 2016 Wu--Xu--Zhu manuscript was not inspected in full.
The stronger stochastic-domination form of BHM is not addressed.
No sharp universal expectation-gap bound depending only on n is claimed.
Independent audit has not been performed.
